senses.definition: To open your mouth wide and breathe in deeply, often without planning to because you feel tired.
senses.example: I yawned halfway through the second story.

senses.definition: The act of opening your mouth wide and breathing in deeply, often when tired.
senses.example: I covered my mouth during a long yawn.

senses.definition: A period of about 365 days, or the period covering January through December on a calendar.
senses.example: We took a picture in the same place each year.

senses.definition: A kind of tiny fungus. Bread yeast can use sugars and release carbon dioxide gas.
senses.example: Yeast made bubbles that swelled the bread dough.

senses.definition: To say or call something in a loud voice.
senses.example: We yelled to our friends across the field.

senses.definition: A loud sound made with the voice.
senses.example: A yell from the bench told us who had scored.

senses.definition: A color like that of a lemon peel or a ripe banana peel.
senses.example: I used yellow for the edge of the kite.

senses.definition: Having a color like that of a lemon peel or a ripe banana peel.
senses.example: The yellow school bus stopped at the corner.

senses.definition: To become or make something turn yellow.
senses.example: Old paper can yellow over time.

senses.definition: Up to the present time, or before the time being talked about.
senses.example: We have not found the last key yet.

senses.definition: Used to tell that there is more of something, often unexpectedly.
senses.example: I found yet another missing game piece under the couch.

senses.definition: Used to connect two things that seem to go against each other.
senses.example: It rained all morning, yet the path was almost dry by noon.
The apple trees yielded enough fruit for ten pies.

senses.definition: To give way or let someone else go first.
senses.example: Bicycles must yield to people crossing the path here.
Our garden had a big yield of beans this year.

senses.definition: A soft, slightly sour food made when certain helpful bacteria change milk.
senses.example: I stirred berries into plain yogurt.

senses.definition: In the early part of life or of the time something has existed.
senses.example: The young tree needed a stake to hold it straight.

senses.definition: The babies or offspring of animals, usually used as the young or their young.
senses.example: The robins brought food to their young.

senses.definition: Used before a noun to show that the thing belongs to or is connected with the person or people being spoken to.
senses.example: Please put your paper in the blue tray.
